protocol.method: Whole-frame read at 25% of each finished 2048x2048 Artifact Master, a full-size 100% pass over the object and its immediate surroundings, and 200-300% re-checks on the highest-risk areas per object (engraved lettering, engraved numerals, quill barb and spine detail, mirror filigree, die pips, whistle tracery, card faces, revolver scroll engraving, crucifix relief and rays). Texture, seam and clipping checks were run on the same master.
protocol.repair_basis: No masked local repair was applied. The approved sources arrive without local damage, the finishing order contains no generative step beyond one super-resolution pass, and every stage output is derivable from the locked source and the recorded grade parameters.

A01.primary_read: an ornate silver hand mirror standing on a dark wooden table, its glass holding a rippling half-seen scene
A01.secondary_read: an occult instrument that watches; the reflection is not a plain reflection of the room
A01.generic_fantasy_read: bounded Victorian occult still life; not generic fantasy ornament
A01.crop_safety_note: The approved source is already 1254x1254, so the 1:1 crop removes no pixels; the mirror frame, stand and table edge all sit inside the frame with margin.
A01.readability_note: Frame filigree, the cast scroll feet and the reflected window mullions stay individually readable at 100%; the glass ripple reads as a surface rather than as blur.
A01.detail_note: The mirror glass keeps its gradient at 200% and does not posterize into bands; highlight clipping stays inside the recorded budget.
A01.seam_note: No super-resolution tile seam, halo or staircase artefact along the frame rim or the glass edge.
A01.text_like_glyph_check: No letter, numeral or pseudo-writing is legible at 100% or 200%.
A01.structural_repetition_check: No repeated tile or foliage pattern introduced by the upscale.
A01.canon_consistency_note: The finished object reads as a silver mirror that displays a scene, which is the only form claim verified from a primary page for this object.
